chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Whoever washes a dead person should perform ghusl. I said: If he touches him while he is still warm? He said: Then there is no ghusl upon him; but when he has become cold and then he touches him, he should perform ghusl. I said: What about the one who places him into the grave? He said: There is no ghusl upon him; he only touches the clothes.
ai.seo_question: When does touching a dead body require ghusl in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ghusl related to contact with the deceased. It states that one who washes a dead body performs ghusl, and that touching the corpse after it has become cold necessitates ghusl, whereas touching it while still warm or placing it into the grave does not.
